stem:
Kiara sets up a half-leaf bottle experiment on a destarched green leaf. Part X of the leaf is enclosed in a bottle so it cannot get carbon dioxide from air. Part Y stays in open air with carbon dioxide. Both parts get water and sunlight. Oxygen is also present around the leaf. She later tests both parts with iodine.

Answer both parts.

options.text: Carbon dioxide from air is essential for the leaf to prepare starch, so Part Y should turn blue-black with iodine and Part X should not.
Oxygen from air is essential for the leaf to prepare starch.
Water and sunlight alone are enough for Part X to prepare starch without carbon dioxide.
Making starch produces the carbon dioxide around the leaf.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Only the half that can get carbon dioxide from air can make starch; the enclosed half lacks carbon dioxide so it should not turn blue-black with iodine.

teacher.key_rationale: The half-leaf bottle experiment shows carbon dioxide is needed for starch formation. Oxygen is not the gas being withheld here; water and sunlight alone are not enough; starch-making does not produce the carbon dioxide supply.
